summary: This work demonstrates efficient multi-qubit entangling operations on a superconducting quantum processor with a central reconfigurable router, achieving three- and four-qubit W states with fidelities $ac{97.72(3)\\\\ \text{%}$ and $94.70(4)\\\\ \text{%}$ in single-step interactions, and using model-free reinforcement learning (PPO) to synthesize native three-qubit gates. The RL-trained controlled-Z gate reaches $96.56 \text{ %} \pm 0.12 \text{ %}$ fidelity (25 % infidelity reduction versus hand-tuned), while the controlled-SWAP and controlled-controlled-phase gates achieve $85.74(78) \text{ %}$ and $84.59(75) \text{ %}$ respectively, outperforming decomposition into two-qubit gates.
motivation: Multi-qubit native gates offer higher parallelism and reduced gate counts compared to decompositions into Clifford gates, enabling faster quantum error correction cycles and more complex algorithms on near-term processors where gate depth and decoherence dominate performance.
method: Using simultaneous dynamic tuning of four reconfigurable switches in a central router to mediate many-to-many couplings, the authors prepare multi-qubit states via single-excitation evolution, synthesize entangling gates through flux-pulse optimization with the PPO reinforcement learning algorithm integrated with cross-entropy benchmarking (OXEBIT method), and encode control in piecewise-constant pulse segments with 8 samples per pulse.
result: Three-qubit W and GHZ states prepared in $9.3$ and $19.6$ ns achieve higher fidelity than prior sequential methods (97.72 % vs. 93.87 % for three qubits); RL-optimized CZ gate surpasses hand-tuned performance with 96.56 % fidelity; three-qubit CSWAP (85.74 %) outperforms estimated decomposition fidelity below 75 %; decoherence limits gate errors at 8–10 % out of total 14–15 % infidelity, with training requiring $\sim 2000$ epochs ($\sim 19$ hours wall time for CZ).
